title: Adult unlawful cultivation of more than six cannabis plants
summary: For a person age 18 or older, unlawfully planting, cultivating, harvesting, drying or processing more than six living cannabis plants under subdivisions (c)-(d). Exactly six plants does not satisfy this greater-than-six branch. Under-18 cases and the age-18-to-20 six-or-fewer infraction are outside this entry. Lawful adult-use, medical and licensed commercial activity must be distinguished from unlawful conduct. A license alone does not excuse acts outside its state/local authorization and governing requirements.
penalty: Ordinary subdivision (c): up to 6 months in county jail, a fine up to $500, or both. Subdivision (d) permits a felony term of 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under Penal Code section 1170(h) only for a qualifying serious/registrable prior, two or more prior subdivision (c) convictions, or the specified environmental conditions in (d)(3). Those conditions require the listed statutory violation or intentional/grossly negligent substantial environmental harm; an environmental concern alone is insufficient. Terms under Penal Code section 1170(h) are ordinarily served in county jail, subject to its state-prison exclusions. The $500 figure is the ordinary subdivision (c) fine, not a complete calculation for a felony case. A drug-program fee up to $150 under section 11372.7 depends on ability to pay. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, restitution, assessments and case-specific sentencing rules may change the result.
mentalState: Knowing unlawful cultivation and the adult-age/plant-count conditions; a felony branch requires its additional statutory facts.

title: Adult unlawful possession of cannabis for sale
summary: For a person age 18 or older, knowingly possessing a usable amount of cannabis with intent that it be unlawfully sold. Possession for personal use is not possession for sale. Under-18 cases use a separate route. Lawful adult-use, medical and licensed commercial activity must be distinguished from unlawful conduct. A license alone does not excuse acts outside its state/local authorization and governing requirements.
penalty: Ordinary subdivision (b): up to 6 months in county jail, a fine up to $500, or both. A 16-month, 2-year or 3-year felony term under section 1170(h) is possible under (c) for a qualifying serious/registrable prior, two prior (b) convictions, or knowing sale/attempted sale to a minor. Subdivision (d) separately covers an actor age 21 or older knowingly using a person age 20 or younger in the specified unlawful cannabis activities. Terms under Penal Code section 1170(h) are ordinarily served in county jail, subject to its state-prison exclusions. Section 11372(a) also lists this offense for an additional fine up to $20,000; the $500 ordinary fine is not presented as an all-in monetary ceiling. A drug-program fee up to $150 under section 11372.7 depends on ability to pay. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, restitution, assessments and case-specific sentencing rules may change the result.
mentalState: Knowledge of the cannabis and intent to sell; each higher-penalty age, prior-conviction or knowing-minor-sale condition must be established.

title: Adult unlawful cannabis sale, distribution, import or transport for sale
summary: For a person age 18 or older, unlawfully selling, furnishing, administering, giving away, importing or transporting cannabis for sale, or making the specified offers or attempts. Transport requires a sale purpose; moving personal-use cannabis is not enough. An offer requires intent to carry it out. The separate (b) small-quantity, nonconcentrated-cannabis giveaway/transport infraction must not be assigned the (a) penalty. Lawful adult-use, medical and licensed commercial activity must be distinguished from unlawful conduct. A license alone does not excuse acts outside its state/local authorization and governing requirements.
penalty: Ordinary subdivision (a)(2): up to 6 months in county jail, a fine up to $500, or both. Subdivision (a)(3) permits a 2-, 3- or 4-year felony term under section 1170(h) for a qualifying serious/registrable prior, two prior (a)(2) convictions, the specified knowing minor-related acts, or the specified interstate import/export acts involving more than 28.5 grams of cannabis or more than 4 grams of concentrate. The interstate concentrate threshold is 4 grams, not the 8-gram personal-possession threshold. Terms under Penal Code section 1170(h) are ordinarily served in county jail, subject to its state-prison exclusions. Section 11372(a) also lists this offense for an additional fine up to $20,000; the $500 ordinary fine is not an all-in monetary ceiling. A drug-program fee up to $150 under section 11372.7 depends on ability to pay. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, restitution, assessments and case-specific sentencing rules may change the result.
mentalState: Knowledge of the cannabis and unlawful act; sale intent for transport and intent to perform an offer. Any felony-triggering facts require separate proof.

title: Possession of specified PCP precursors with intent to manufacture
summary: Knowingly possessing the specific chemical combinations, compounds, mixtures, isomers or sufficient immediate precursors covered by subdivisions (a)-(d), with intent to manufacture PCP or the analog specified by the applicable branch. Different branches cover different substances; possession of an ordinary chemical without the required manufacture intent is insufficient. Licensed manufacturers and persons authorized by Board of Pharmacy regulation are excluded.
penalty: Felony: 2, 4 or 6 years under Penal Code section 1170(h). Terms under Penal Code section 1170(h) are ordinarily served in county jail, subject to its state-prison exclusions. Penal Code section 672 permits an additional fine up to $10,000 for a felony when no other fine is prescribed. A drug-program fee up to $150 under section 11372.7 depends on ability to pay. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, restitution, assessments and case-specific sentencing rules may change the result.
mentalState: Knowing possession, the specified substance or combination and the particular manufacture or transfer intent; recipient-manufacture knowledge is separately required for sections 11383.6 and 11383.7.

title: Possessing or using a vehicle false compartment for controlled substances
summary: Possessing, using or controlling a false compartment in or attached to a vehicle with intent to store, conceal, smuggle or transport a controlled substance in it. Under the definition reflected in CALCRIM 2441 and People v. Arias, original factory equipment must be modified, altered or supplemented; merely hiding drugs in an unchanged factory space is not enough. Vehicle includes aircraft, boats and other listed conveyances.
penalty: Misdemeanor alternative: up to 364 days in county jail. Felony alternative: 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under section 1170(h). Terms under Penal Code section 1170(h) are ordinarily served in county jail, subject to its state-prison exclusions. Penal Code section 672 permits an additional fine up to $1,000 for a misdemeanor or $10,000 for a felony when no other fine is prescribed. A drug-program fee up to $150 under section 11372.7 depends on ability to pay. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, restitution, assessments and case-specific sentencing rules may change the result.
mentalState: Intent to store, conceal, smuggle or transport a controlled substance in the qualifying false compartment; innocent construction or use is insufficient.

title: Constructing or installing a vehicle false compartment for controlled substances
summary: Designing, constructing, building, altering, fabricating, installing or attaching a false compartment for or to a vehicle, with intent to store, conceal, smuggle or transport a controlled substance in it. The qualifying alteration/addition to factory equipment matters; this does not criminalize an unchanged ordinary vehicle storage space.
penalty: Felony: 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under section 1170(h). Terms under Penal Code section 1170(h) are ordinarily served in county jail, subject to its state-prison exclusions. Penal Code section 672 permits an additional fine up to $10,000 for a felony when no other fine is prescribed. A drug-program fee up to $150 under section 11372.7 depends on ability to pay. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, restitution, assessments and case-specific sentencing rules may change the result.
mentalState: Intent to store, conceal, smuggle or transport a controlled substance in the qualifying false compartment; innocent construction or use is insufficient.

title: Possession of more than $100,000 in drug proceeds or money for an unlawful drug purchase
summary: Two distinct theories: knowingly possessing more than $100,000 in money or negotiable instruments obtained from the specified unlawful drug activity; or possessing more than $100,000 intended for an unlawful drug purchase and committing an act in substantial furtherance of that purchase. Exactly $100,000 is insufficient. For an attorney accepting a criminal-investigation/proceeding fee, subdivision (b) additionally requires intent to participate in the unlawful conduct or disguise its source/nature; receiving a fee alone is insufficient.
penalty: Misdemeanor alternative: up to 364 days in county jail. Felony alternative: 2, 3 or 4 years under section 1170(h). Terms under Penal Code section 1170(h) are ordinarily served in county jail, subject to its state-prison exclusions. Penal Code section 672 permits an additional fine up to $1,000 for a misdemeanor or $10,000 for a felony when no other fine is prescribed. A drug-program fee up to $150 under section 11372.7 depends on ability to pay. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, restitution, assessments and case-specific sentencing rules may change the result.
mentalState: Proceeds theory: knowledge of the unlawful source. Purchase theory: intent to make an unlawful purchase plus a substantial-furtherance act. The special attorney-fee intent rule must be preserved.

title: Offering to manufacture a controlled substance
summary: Offering to manufacture, compound, convert, produce, derive, process or prepare a scheduled controlled substance by the chemical-extraction or chemical-synthesis means in subdivision (a), with intent to carry out the offer. A completed manufacturing operation is not required. The retained statute puts this offense in (e), although CALCRIM 2331 still cites (c).
penalty: Felony: 3, 4 or 5 years under section 1170(h). Terms under Penal Code section 1170(h) are ordinarily served in county jail, subject to its state-prison exclusions. Penal Code section 672 permits an additional fine up to $10,000 for a felony when no other fine is prescribed. A drug-program fee up to $150 under section 11372.7 depends on ability to pay. The manufacturing offense in (a) has a different 3/5/7-year term and a fine up to $50,000; those are not substituted for this offer branch. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, restitution, assessments and case-specific sentencing rules may change the result.
mentalState: An offer and intent to perform the unlawful manufacture, including the required knowledge of controlled character.

title: Being under the influence of specified drugs while possessing a loaded firearm
summary: Unlawfully being under the influence of cocaine, cocaine base, heroin, methamphetamine or PCP while in immediate personal possession of a loaded, operable firearm. The statute includes a motor vehicle passenger compartment within immediate personal possession. It requires being under the influence, not merely possessing a drug; the separate armed-possession offense is section 11370.1.
penalty: First-conviction alternatives: up to 364 days in county jail or 16 months, 2 years or 3 years in state prison. Under (f), a second or later conviction under (e) carries 2, 3 or 4 years in state prison. Penal Code section 672 permits an additional fine up to $1,000 for a misdemeanor or $10,000 for a felony when no other fine is prescribed. Subdivision (d) permits an additional fine up to $70, subject to ability to pay. The specified deferred-entry/preguilty-plea drug-court route is unavailable for (e) under (g); this is not a blanket determination of eligibility for every other program. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, restitution, assessments and case-specific sentencing rules may change the result.
mentalState: Unlawful influence of one of the listed drugs and immediate personal possession of an actually loaded, operable firearm.

title: Using fortified premises for specified unlawful drug activity
summary: Using a building, room, space or enclosure specifically designed to suppress law-enforcement entry, for selling, manufacturing or possessing for sale one of the listed drugs. The list includes cocaine/cocaine base, heroin, PCP, amphetamine, methamphetamine and LSD. This differs from a premises owner merely making property available under section 11366.5.
penalty: Felony: 3, 4 or 5 years under section 1170(h). Terms under Penal Code section 1170(h) are ordinarily served in county jail, subject to its state-prison exclusions. Penal Code section 672 permits an additional fine up to $10,000 for a felony when no other fine is prescribed. A drug-program fee up to $150 under section 11372.7 depends on ability to pay. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, restitution, assessments and case-specific sentencing rules may change the result.
mentalState: Use of the specially designed premises for the specified unlawful drug purpose; fortification alone does not establish every element.

title: Retail or wholesale sale of supplies for unlawful drug manufacture
summary: A retailer or wholesaler sells a chemical, drug, laboratory apparatus or device knowing or intending that it will be used to unlawfully manufacture, compound, convert, process or prepare a controlled substance for unlawful sale or distribution. Ordinary supply sales without the required knowledge or intent are outside this offense.
penalty: Up to 364 days in county jail, or 16 months, 2 years or 3 years in state prison; a fine up to $25,000; or both imprisonment and the fine. A drug-program fee up to $150 under section 11372.7 depends on ability to pay. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, restitution, assessments and case-specific sentencing rules may change the result.
mentalState: The seller must be a retailer or wholesaler and have knowledge or intent concerning the specified unlawful manufacture for sale/distribution.

title: Receiving or transacting in unlawful drug proceeds
summary: Knowingly receiving or acquiring proceeds, or engaging in a transaction involving proceeds, known to be derived from an offense under the specified controlled-substance divisions, with intent to conceal/disguise or help conceal/disguise the specified attributes, or to avoid a state or federal reporting requirement. Under (f), the transaction or related transactions within 30 days must involve over $25,000, or the proceeds must exceed $25,000; exactly $25,000 is insufficient. Subdivision (g) excludes the specified criminal-defense advice/representation fees received by an attorney.
penalty: Misdemeanor alternative: up to 364 days in county jail. State-prison alternative: 2, 3 or 4 years. A fine up to $250,000 or twice the value of the proceeds/property, whichever is greater, may be imposed alone or with imprisonment. Each violation can be separately punished. A drug-program fee up to $150 under section 11372.7 depends on ability to pay. Adult base penalties are shown; enhancements, restitution, assessments and case-specific sentencing rules may change the result.
mentalState: Knowledge of the unlawful source or intended unlawful use, the specified act, and intent to conceal/disguise or avoid reporting. A large transaction by itself is insufficient.
